v.description: Schema major version of the primitive. Unknown majors render fallback_text.

id.description: Widget id, unique per gateway: w_ + 6–40 letters or digits. The directive references it.

rev.description: Revision, starting at 1. An update replaces the payload with a higher rev; the client shows the newest.

state_label.description: The word in the state badge when the default isn’t right: “92%”, “Needs your OK”, “On time”.

stale_after.description: Seconds after as_of when the data counts as stale.

fallback_text.description: The plain-text version: complete, readable on its own, used by every client that can’t render the widget and by Copy as Text. ≤ 2,000 characters for one widget (each type schema enforces it); ≤ 4,000 for a stack.

summary.description: One line for VoiceOver, chat previews and notifications (unless private). Defaults to title + state.

text.description: One line that must be read before the body: “2 ingredients have no allergen data, so this can’t be called safe.”

banner.description: The card banner (Parts.cardBanner). Stale and expired banners are drawn by the client; don’t send them.

empty_text.description: The sentence shown when there is nothing to show, in the primitive’s words: “No open tickets. Inbox zero.” Defaults to the primitive’s own empty sentence.

sensitivity.description: private: kept out of previews, notifications, Spotlight and group chats.

producer.description: Who made it. Set by the plugin from the session, never by the agent; the header always shows the real sender.

in_reply_to.description: The widget this one answers (a receipt for an approval).

supersedes.description: An older widget this one replaces: its id, or task:<task id> for the newest widget the same scheduled task sent to this chat (the plugin resolves it). The client folds the older card to one line and disables its actions.

user.description: The gateway user id, when known.

for.description: Who may answer, in a group chat. Defaults to the chat’s owner; others see the widget read-only (“For Alex”).

locale.description: BCP 47 language of the text, when it isn’t the reader’s.
